name: epubcheck-standalone
description: EPUBCheck, the official W3C EPUB validator, compiled to plain JavaScript with TeaVM: an embeddable library that validates EPUBs in Node.js and the browser with byte-identical output to the Java tool, no Java to install.

scripts.//: Repo commands opt into the custom `epubcheck-standalone:source` export condition and run the TypeScript sources directly. Published consumers do not set that condition and resolve the Rolldown-built dist/ files.
scripts.//test: EPUBCHECK_REQUIRE_JAR=1 is exported so the jar-backed suites (flags, custom-messages, url) FAIL rather than skip-and-pass when the jar+java are absent: this repo's dev flow always has them (the engine build needs them). Jar-less consumers unset it to get the graceful skip.
scripts.test: export EPUBCHECK_REQUIRE_JAR=1 && node test/smoke.ts && node test/validate.ts && node test/fs-async.ts && node test/plugins-async.ts && node test/tap-coverage.ts && node test/reuse.ts && node test/memory-plateau.ts && node test/engine-error-cleanup.ts && node test/abort.ts && node test/abort-suspension.ts && node test/parity.ts && node test/reports.ts && node test/formatters.ts && node test/console.ts && node test/flags.ts && node test/expanded.ts && node test/custom-messages.ts && node test/url.ts && node test/s3.ts && node test/plugins-name-defaulting.ts && node test/http-bridge.ts
scripts.//test:reports:generate: Regenerate the committed report ground truth with the real epubcheck.jar (needs a jar + java: set EPUBCHECK_JAR / EPUBCHECK_JAVA, or run `npm run build:deps` first and let it resolve the mise GraalVM). Writes test/expected-reports/<sub>/<book>.epub.{json,xml,xmp} for every .epub under test/corpus, which is what test/reports.ts checks byte-for-byte. Pass `-- --existing-only` to only refresh books that already have expected reports (how update-epubcheck.yml keeps the committed set at its current size).
scripts.//test:parity:generate: Rebuild the committed JAR CONSOLE ANSWER KEYS by running the real epubcheck.jar ONCE per book in test/corpus (testing/build-console-cache.ts). From that single merged `2>&1` run it writes BOTH: (1) test/expected/<group>.json -- the sorted, order-insensitive MESSAGE cache test/parity.ts checks, and (2) test/expected-console-ordered/<group>.json -- the ORDERED full console text test/console.ts checks byte-for-byte. Both are the jar's output, NOT captured from our engine. Needs a jar + java (set EPUBCHECK_JAR / EPUBCHECK_JAVA, or run `npm run build:deps` first); hard-fails if absent. Bump-only: the git diff of both caches is the console behavioral-drift review.
scripts.//test:cache:build: Rebuild ALL committed jar answer keys in one go -- the console MESSAGE cache (test/expected) + the ORDERED console cache (test/expected-console-ordered), both from the single build-console-cache.ts run, and the report cache (test/expected-reports) for ALL books. This is the whole answer key the engine-vs-cache suites (parity, console, reports, formatters) compare against; run it only when epubcheck's Java version bumps and review the resulting git diff. It also folds in what the retired live upstream-sweep used to do: the jar's answers are captured once, here, instead of recomputed live on every compare.
scripts.test:cache:build: npm run test:parity:generate && npm run test:reports:generate
scripts.//test:pack-consumer: Packs the library with `npm pack` and exercises the tarball as a real consumer (fresh install, ESM import, validate a fixture, typecheck against the shipped .d.ts). Runs build:ts itself and needs the built engine present plus network for the consumer install, so it lives outside the `test` chain -- run it before publishing.
